ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Megan
Quigley.

Using data to understand disparities.
Turning policies and benefits into practical support.

≠

From analysis to access.

Megan’s work spans workforce analysis, financial wellness benefits, and guidance for people navigating workplace transitions. At NBCUniversal, she examined compensation and promotion disparities. At Lincoln Financial, she helped build benefits that connect employees with financial support.

Available ≠ Accessible brings that perspective to public benefits: what stands between a program’s promise and a person’s ability to use it? The project combines verified public data, research, and visual storytelling to examine gaps in WIC, housing, and Medicaid access.

Her professional experience informs the questions. The findings come from the public research cited throughout the site.

ABOUT THIS PROJECT

Research made visible.

Megan researches and develops Available ≠ Accessible, using verified public data and AI-assisted development to build scroll-driven stories about benefit access. The project maps barriers, explains what the evidence can tell us, and connects readers with benefit resources.

This independent project synthesizes published research. It does not present original interviews or national survey findings and is not affiliated with the programs discussed.
